summary_rationale: SoftTech Engineers owns real product intellectual property in building-permit automation, with a long installed base among Indian urban local bodies, 40% revenue growth in FY2026, fast-growing pay-per-use revenue, and a new infrastructure and transferable-development-rights product line. The audited record is much weaker than the revenue story. Group profit after tax of ₹5.3 crore in FY2026 is below FY2019 on a larger share count. Free cash flow was negative in every year from FY2019 to FY2026 because operating cash is re-spent on capitalised software, and the five years to FY2026 were funded by about ₹83 crore of new equity. Receivables and unbilled contract assets equal about 240 days of revenue, 42% of gross trade receivables are over a year old, and the credit-loss charge was larger than group pre-tax profit. Return on invested capital is about 4%, the auditor's report records bank-return mismatches, and the claimed 80% share of the permit niche is undocumented while Telangana replaced the company's platform with a rival and a free government platform now competes. The business is conditional on three proofs: collections converting to cash, amortisation catching up with capitalised development without erasing profit, and large infrastructure orders repeating rather than arriving once. Until those appear, this is a promising software franchise with unproven cash economics, not a proven compounder.
